issue: Reece Plumbing Supply invoice 88412 is entered twice, and BT-0051 is the copy that is not on the bank statement.
proposed_fix: Delete or void BT-0051 ($1,848.00, including GST of $168.00). Keep BT-0050, which is matched to SL-0050. This removes $1,680.00 of duplicated Materials (310) and a $168.00 duplicated GST credit.
evidence: BT-0050: Contact Reece Plumbing Supply, Date 2026-08-11, Reference "INV 88412", Total 1848.00, LineAmount 1680.00, TaxAmount 168.00, IsReconciled true, matched by SL-0050 (2026-08-11, REECE PLUMBING SUPPLY, -1848.00). BT-0051: Contact Reece Plumbing Supply, Date 2026-08-12, Reference "88412", Total 1848.00, LineAmount 1680.00, TaxAmount 168.00, IsReconciled false. No statement line is matched to BT-0051.

issue: A laptop costing more than the $1,000 capitalise threshold was expensed to Repairs and Maintenance instead of being recorded as a fixed asset.
proposed_fix: Recode the line from 473 Repairs and Maintenance to 720 Computer Equipment (fixed asset), LineAmount 2,635.45 ex-GST, and depreciate it from August 2026. Leave the GST treatment (INPUT, 263.55) to the GST reviewer.
evidence: BT-0046, 2026-08-16, Contact JB Hi-Fi Business (DefaultAccountCode 720), Description "Laptop for estimator", AccountCode 473, TaxType INPUT, LineAmount 2635.45, TaxAmount 263.55, Total 2899.00. Organisation Policies.CapitaliseThreshold 1000.0. A laptop lasts more than a year.

issue: The Coastal Electrical Contractors transaction is recorded at $1,254.00, but the bank statement line it is matched to shows $1,524.00, which looks like transposed digits.
proposed_fix: Check the Coastal Electrical progress claim invoice for job J-124. If the invoice is $1,524.00 (as the bank shows), correct BT-0052 to Total $1,524.00 (LineAmount $1,385.45, GST $138.55) and reconcile it again. If the invoice is $1,254.00, the supplier was overpaid by $270.00: ask Coastal Electrical for a refund or credit note.
evidence: SL-0051: Date 2026-08-24, Payee COASTAL ELECTRICAL CON, Amount -1524.00, MatchedTransactionID BT-0052. BT-0052: Date 2026-08-24, Contact Coastal Electrical Contractors, "Progress claim, job J-124", AccountCode 315, LineAmount 1140.00, TaxAmount 114.00, Total 1254.00, IsReconciled true. The difference is $270.00.

issue: An installation charge from a subcontractor was coded to Materials instead of Subcontractors, which puts the J-118 job cost split out.
proposed_fix: Recode the line from 310 Materials to 315 Subcontractors, LineAmount 5,800.00 ex-GST (Total 6,380.00), keeping job J-118. If the invoice shows supplied materials separately, split out only that part to 310.
evidence: BT-0047, 2026-08-22, Contact Pinewood Joinery (DefaultAccountCode 315; other Pinewood lines BT-0030, BT-0031, BT-0033 coded 315), Description "Joinery install, job J-118", AccountCode 310, TaxType INPUT, LineAmount 5800.00, TaxAmount 580.00, Total 6380.00.

issue: An $8,420.00 ATO payment on the bank statement has no transaction in Xero, so it is missing from the books.
proposed_fix: This is most likely a BAS payment (GST, PAYG withholding and/or PAYG instalment) for a prior period. Ask the client for the ATO integrated client account statement or the BAS/payment slip showing the $8,420.00 split. Then record a spend transaction (BAS Excluded) against the ATO clearing, GST and PAYG liability accounts, and reconcile it to SL-0052.
evidence: SL-0052: Date 2026-08-28, Payee ATO PAYMENT, Amount -8420.00, MatchedTransactionID null. No Xero bank transaction for the period has an ATO contact or a total of 8420.00.

issue: A Woolworths grocery purchase on the company account was coded to Entertainment and looks like private spending.
proposed_fix: Ask the client whether the groceries had a business purpose. If they did not, recode the full 214.35 to 880 Owner A Drawings, BAS Excluded, with no GST credit (the GST reviewer will pick up the 19.49 credit separately).
evidence: BT-0048, 2026-08-23, Contact Woolworths, Description "Groceries", AccountCode 420 Entertainment, TaxType INPUT, LineAmount 194.86, TaxAmount 19.49, Total 214.35.

issue: Commonwealth Bank merchant facility fee is coded to Bank Fees with a GST credit, but bank fees are input taxed under the firm's rules, so no GST credit can be claimed.
proposed_fix: Change TaxType from INPUT to EXEMPTEXPENSES (input taxed, account 404 default). LineAmount 64.90, TaxAmount 0.00, reversing the 5.90 GST credit.
evidence: BT-0042, 2026-08-31, SPEND, Contact Commonwealth Bank, Description 'Merchant facility fee', AccountCode 404 (Bank Fees, default TaxType EXEMPTEXPENSES), TaxType INPUT, LineAmount 59.00, TaxAmount 5.90, Total 64.90. The matching account-keeping fee BT-0041 is correctly EXEMPTEXPENSES with TaxAmount 0.00.

issue: A 12-month insurance premium that covers August 2026 to July 2027 was expensed in full in August instead of being recorded as a prepayment.
proposed_fix: Recode the 4,800.00 ex-GST amount from 433 Insurance to 620 Prepayments and keep the GST credit of 480.00 in August. Release 400.00 a month (4,800.00 / 12) from 620 to 433 from August 2026 to July 2027. After August's release, 433 carries 400.00 and 620 has 4,400.00 left.
evidence: BT-0049, 2026-08-02, Contact QBE Insurance, Description "Contract works insurance, 12 months to 31 Jul 2027", AccountCode 433, TaxType INPUT, LineAmount 4800.00, TaxAmount 480.00, Total 5280.00. Organisation Policies.CapitaliseThreshold 1000.0 (the premium is above it).

issue: A GST credit of $360.00 was claimed on a payment to Ridge Tiling, but the supplier is not registered for GST, so the line should be GST free and the credit reversed.
proposed_fix: Change TaxType from INPUT to GST Free (EXEMPTEXPENSES / no GST). LineAmount 3,960.00, TaxAmount 0.00, reversing the 360.00 credit. If Ridge Tiling's invoice shows GST, ask the client to get a corrected invoice, because an unregistered supplier cannot charge GST.
evidence: BT-0043, 2026-08-26, SPEND, Contact 'Ridge Tiling (sole trader)' (C006, TaxNumber 71 824 330 016, IsGSTRegistered false), Description 'Tiling, job J-121', AccountCode 315, TaxType INPUT, LineAmount 3600.00, TaxAmount 360.00, Total 3960.00.

issue: Casual wages are coded with a GST credit (INPUT), but wages are BAS Excluded, so no GST credit is available.
proposed_fix: Change TaxType from INPUT to BASEXCLUDED. LineAmount 3,300.00, TaxAmount 0.00, reversing the 300.00 credit.
evidence: BT-0044, 2026-08-17, SPEND, Contact Payroll Clearing (C020, IsGSTRegistered false, no ABN), Description 'Weekly wages (casual)', AccountCode 477 (Wages and Salaries, default BASEXCLUDED), TaxType INPUT, LineAmount 3000.00, TaxAmount 300.00, Total 3300.00. The other wage runs (BT-0001 to BT-0005) are BASEXCLUDED with TaxAmount 0.00.

issue: GST was worked out as 10% of the GST-inclusive total ($217.80) rather than Total / 11 ($198.00), so the credit is overstated by $19.80.
proposed_fix: Set TaxAmount to 198.00 and LineAmount to 1,980.00 (Total stays 2,178.00). This reduces the GST credit by 19.80.
evidence: BT-0045, 2026-08-09, SPEND, Contact Laminex Direct (IsGSTRegistered true), Description 'Benchtop laminate, job J-124', AccountCode 310, TaxType INPUT, LineAmount 1960.20, TaxAmount 217.80, Total 2178.00. 2178.00 / 11 = 198.00; 2178.00 x 10% = 217.80.

issue: A GST credit of $19.49 was claimed on Woolworths groceries, which look like private spending, and private spending gets no GST credit.
proposed_fix: If the client confirms the purchase is private, change TaxType from INPUT to BASEXCLUDED (in line with the move to Owner A Drawings 880 that the coding reviewer will raise). LineAmount 214.35, TaxAmount 0.00, reversing the 19.49 credit. Ask the client whether the groceries had a business purpose, such as staff amenities or a client function.
evidence: BT-0048, 2026-08-23, SPEND, Contact Woolworths, Description 'Groceries', AccountCode 420 (Entertainment), TaxType INPUT, LineAmount 194.86, TaxAmount 19.49, Total 214.35.
